promise: Optimus robots will reach volume production in 2026
description: At Tesla's June 2025 shareholder meeting Musk said Optimus would go from low production in 2025 to mass production in 2026. As of mid-2026, Optimus remained in factory-trial/prototype stages, far below the promised production volumes.
evidence: 2025-2026 footage shows Optimus prototypes doing factory tasks, not mass production
Tesla has not reported volume Optimus output as of mid-2026

promise: Brazil will be off the hunger map by the end of my term
description: Lula pledged to remove Brazil from the UN hunger map by the end of his term (Dec 2026). Severe food insecurity fell dramatically (from ~33 million people in 2022 to roughly 9 million by 2025 per IBGE), but Brazil was not formally removed from the FAO's hunger classifications as of mid-2026, with the target still in progress.
evidence: IBGE 2025 data shows sharp drop in severe food insecurity
FAO/UN hunger map status still pending as of mid-2026

description: At Computex 2024 Huang unveiled the Vera Rubin platform (Rubin GPU + Vera CPU) and said it would arrive in 2026, with Rubin Ultra following in 2027. As of mid-2026 it is still scheduled for release in Q3 2026, though Bloomberg reported in Aug 2025 that mass production could slip ~3 months to mid-2026. Deadline has not yet passed.
evidence: Announced at Computex in Taipei in 2024 by Jensen Huang
Wikipedia's Rubin article: 'scheduled for release in Q3 of 2026'
Bloomberg (Aug 2025) reported a possible delay to mid-2026; NVIDIA denied
Rubin Ultra promised for 2027 at GTC 2025

promise: "You might see a smaller jump from GPT-5 to GPT-6 than from GPT-4 to GPT-5" — signaling GPT-6 within roughly a year of GPT-5, i.e., 2026
description: Throughout 2025 Altman told interviewers and DevDay audiences that GPT-6 would follow GPT-5 (released Aug 7, 2025) within about a year. As of mid-2026, OpenAI had shipped GPT-5.2 (Dec 2025) and GPT-5.6 but no GPT-6, so the promise remains unfulfilled. Quote wording per 20VC podcast (Sept 2025) coverage; no exact verbatim transcript verified.
evidence: GPT-5 launched Aug 7, 2025 (Wikipedia)
OpenAI shipped GPT-5.2 and GPT-5.6 by Dec 2025, latest models per Wikipedia's OpenAI/GPT-5 pages
No GPT-6 release or announcement found in news feeds as of July 2026
sources: The Verge: All of the updates from OpenAI DevDay 2025 (Oct 6, 2025)

promise: "I think it could come as early as 2026, though there are also ways it could take much longer."
description: In 'Machines of Loving Grace' (published Oct 2024), Amodei defined AGI as models matching 'top humans in most domains' (10^28-10^29 FLOP training scale, ~2027 cluster sizes) and said it could arrive as early as 2026. No such system exists as of mid-2026, though the essay hedged that it 'could take much longer'.
evidence: Exact quote verified from darioamodei.com/machines-of-loving-grace
Essay defines 'powerful AI' and ties scale to projected ~2027 compute clusters
No human-level general AI shipped by mid-2026

promise: "xAI's ultimate goal is to understand the true nature of the universe."
description: Open-ended mission statement from xAI's launch (July 12, 2023) — an explicit research goal, not a dated deliverable. No deadline was ever attached; the mission remains xAI's stated purpose as of 2026, so it is recorded as kept on a year-end assessment horizon.
evidence: xAI launch announcement and FAQ (July 2023) defined the goal as 'understanding the universe'
Mission restated by Musk in xAI interviews through 2025 and remained xAI's stated purpose through 2026

promise: "There will be a new architecture every year" — Rubin shipping in the second half of 2026, Rubin Ultra in 2027
description: At GTC 2025 Huang pledged an annual GPU architecture cadence (Blackwell → Rubin → Rubin Ultra), with Rubin 'in production in the second half of 2026'. Rubin (Vera Rubin, HBM4) was announced at Computex June 2024; Wikipedia lists launch as Q3 2026, with no confirmed delay as of mid-2026.
evidence: Rubin announced at Computex (June 2024); infobox launch '2H 2026' / Q3 2026 (Wikipedia: Rubin)
GTC 2025: Rubin Ultra announced for 2027
No delay reports surfaced by July 2026

promise: Instinct MI450 'Helios' (CDNA Next) to ship in 2026 with roughly 12x the inference performance of MI300X; AI accelerator market to reach $500 billion by 2028
description: At CES 2025, Su unveiled AMD's 2025-2026 accelerator roadmap: MI350 (mid-2025) and the MI450 'Helios' family for 2026 with a claimed ~12x inference uplift over MI300X, plus a $500B AI-accelerator TAM forecast by 2028. MI350X shipped June 2025 as promised; MI450/Helios was still unreleased as of mid-2026 (expected 2H 2026).
evidence: AMD CES 2025 announcement of MI450 'Helios' for 2026 and $500B TAM by 2028
MI350X/MI355X launched June 2025 (Wikipedia: AMD Instinct)
No MI450/Helios release confirmed as of July 2026

promise: BotQ factory would build 12,000 humanoid robots per year; Figure 03 shipping in 2025
description: Adcock announced the 'BotQ' humanoid factory (early 2025) targeting 12,000 units/year and promised Figure 03 for 2025, building on the BMW manufacturing deployment (deal announced Jan 2024). Figure 03 did launch (Oct 2025) and BMW work proceeded, but by June 2026 only ~740 robots were operating — an order of magnitude below the 12k/year capacity promise.
evidence: BotQ announced early 2025, targeting 12,000 humanoids/year (Wikipedia: Figure AI)
Figure 03 released October 2025
June 2026: ~740 robots operating vs ~600 humans at Figure (Wikipedia)

promise: Raise childcare leave benefits so that parents receive 100 percent of take-home pay when both parents take childcare leave
description: In his policy speech to the 217th session of the Diet, Ishiba pledged to support childcare by raising leave benefits to 100 percent of take-home pay when both parents take childcare leave. The measure was announced as a policy direction with implementation dependent on subsequent legislation and budgeting.
evidence: Announced in the 24 January 2025 policy speech to the Diet
Implementation status still pending as of mid-2026

promise: The United States will acquire Greenland — "we need it for international security."
description: Trump first floated buying Greenland in August 2019 and revived the push after returning to office, saying in early 2026 that the US should control the island and threatening economic consequences if Denmark refused to negotiate. Denmark and Greenland's leaders repeatedly rejected the proposal — 'Greenland is not for sale' — including at a July 2026 NATO leaders' meeting.
evidence: Denmark and Greenland rejected the proposal again at the July 2026 NATO summit
No purchase or transfer agreement exists as of mid-2026

promise: Jetson Thor, NVIDIA's humanoid-robot computer, will arrive in 2026
description: At CES 2025 Huang said NVIDIA's Jetson Thor platform for humanoid robots would arrive in 2026. At GTC Taipei on June 1, 2026, NVIDIA launched the Isaac GR00T reference humanoid robot built on the Jetson AGX Thor T5000 (Blackwell architecture), with a Unitree H2 body and Sharpa dexterous hands — delivering the platform within the promised year.
evidence: Jetson AGX Thor T5000 launched in the Isaac GR00T reference robot, June 2026
GTC Taipei keynote confirmed the 'physical AI' platform in 2026
